blocks.text: Why the winner won

content.value: The winner is not a split of A and B. It is the observation that the SAME sentence generates both halves, so the wave does not have to choose. "I could not look" ≠ "the thing is broken" is what s2 teaches a predicate, what the lane slice teaches a required context, and what four screens on the board are already failing at. A wave with one sentence is a wave whose Decide phase can adjudicate slices against a criterion instead of a wishlist — and it satisfies the ratio floor with rows chosen on merit rather than on quota.

blocks.text: The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

content.value: THE GATE SLICE MAY BE A NON-DEFECT, AND THE "FIX" MAY BE A WEAKENING.

On a dead server the predicate correctly emitted an INFRA FAULT and the test correctly redded. That is an HONEST red. A wave that makes it green has softened a guard and called it hardening — the exact failure this epic exists to catch, committed by the wave that cites the standing test.

The wave does not green the red. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is correct behaviour and is not touched. The defect is narrower and different: a context that BLOCKS a merge is asking a question whose answer lives on a host outside this repository. The remedy is relocation — the live assertion moves somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the lane — plus a hermetic control that is just as cruel and still proves the contrast the test exists to prove (a live refusal never reaches the ladder;
does). Three wrong fixes are banned by name in the slice brief, because each is green by construction under standing clause 4:

blocks.text: CORRECTION 1 — the lane slice’s finished state as written is unachievable, and three surveyors found it independently

content.value: "No merge-blocking job reaches a host this repository does not own" cannot be built. PR references an active task reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud BY DESIGN and BY POLICY: pr-task-gate.yml:257 GETs the ledger, :202 POSTs a mutation with a repo secret, and the step body converts the script’s exit 2 into exit 1 under the annotation "Ledger unreachable — task backing UNVERIFIED", arguing in its own comment that "the only alternative to red is a green check that verified nothing". docs/ops/merge-gates.md:75 codifies it: ledger outage = a red that says so.
So the repo has ALREADY adjudicated this wave’s question in committed bytes on a blocking gate. The honest defect class is narrower and sharper:

rows.value: SEMANTIC — the gate’s question IS about that host
ACCIDENTAL — a unit test of a predicate makes a live roster call
A YAML COMMENT telling a human to read a solitary red at test 56 as "the ledger was unreachable"

content.value: Exactly one of four required contexts fails the test "a required gate may be red by a third-party host only if it names the condition and has a tested override", and it is Console gate. A ratchet phrased as a prohibition reds pr-task-gate.yml the day it lands and its first act is to be waived — a guard that cannot lose, wearing an exemption. content.value: An independent second reviewer is owed on #9455 before merge.

This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so the dispatch is a manual lead step. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. It was measured once, and it decides whether an honest product FAIL can be silently downgraded to an environment excuse.
